result.note: Tests the October 2026 trade margin cap on anti-cancer drugs: its level, coverage and the Supreme Court hearing that preceded it.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Centre capped trade margins on anti-cancer drugs outside India's existing price-control list. Consider the following statements about this move:
items: The cap applies only to generic and off-patent anti-cancer medicines.
Trade margins are capped at 30 percent of the maximum retail price.
It followed a September 2026 Supreme Court hearing in which judges flagged hospitals marking up cancer drugs tenfold.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the cap covers branded and generic, domestic and imported, and patented and off-patent medicines alike. Official sources estimate prices could fall by up to 70 percent, saving patients INR 25 billion a year, while the Supreme Court had pushed for a uniform 16 percent margin on all medicines.
questions.source: On Thursday, the Centre capped trade margins, the markup added between manufacturer and patient, at 30 percent of the maximum retail price (MRP) for all anti-cancer drugs outside India's existing price-control list.
